notes: Every 'conditions' object is a literal restatement of the corresponding RULES[].match(d, w) predicate from hospitalityKnowledge.js, where d = dish.tags and w = drink.tags.

'chicken-light-drink' and 'crispy-carbonation' are cross-cutting rules in the source code (they also fire for non-wine drinks: any light-bodied pour, or beer). They are included here because a wine (white / sparkling) is the primary/first-listed match branch, but they are NOT wine-exclusive in the original code -- see the same two entries duplicated with a cross-reference note in beer_pairings.json for the beer-facing branch of crispy-carbonation.

phrases.*.text values are copied verbatim from RULES[].clauses[tone] in hospitalityKnowledge.js. The literal '{dish}' placeholder is preserved exactly as in source; it is substituted with the lowercased dish name at render time by whyClauseFor().

Two-variant clause sets are rotated deterministically via pick(list, `${dish.name}|${drink.name}|${rule.id}`) (hashString-based), not randomly -- captured here as 'rotation: deterministic-hash' rather than reimplemented.

entries.principle: tannin+fat: richness/marbling softens tannins, smooths finish

professional: The richness in the {dish} holds up well against a fuller-bodied red — it softens the tannins and gives you a smoother finish.
A full-bodied red like this is built for the char on the {dish}; the tannins settle down against the richness.
friendly: The marbling in the {dish} really works with a fuller-bodied red — you get a much smoother finish.
Honestly the char on the {dish} is made for a red with this much backbone, it just softens everything out.
luxury: The wine's structure comes alive against the richness of the {dish} — the tannins soften and the finish lengthens.
A red with this much depth was built for a cut like the {dish}; the marbling rounds off every tannin.

entries.principle: tannin+fat: same as red-full-rich-meat, but fires for any rich dish (e.g. rich sauce) without a beef/lamb/game protein tag

professional: The richness of the {dish} holds up well against a fuller-bodied red — it softens the tannins nicely.
friendly: That creamy, rich sauce on the {dish} can really take a red with this much weight — it softens everything out.
luxury: A red with this much depth stands up comfortably to the richness of the {dish}.

entries.principle: balance: medium structure rounds out the plate without fighting or overpowering it

professional: A medium-bodied red won't fight with the {dish} — it just rounds the plate out nicely.
friendly: This one's not too heavy, so it just rounds out the {dish} without taking over.
luxury: A softer-structured red like this lets the {dish} lead, rather than competing with it.

entries.principle: acidity lift: acid cuts through / lifts seafood rather than masking it — classic pairing
entries.rotation: deterministic-hash (single-variant clause set, no rotation needed)

professional: The acidity in the wine lifts the seafood rather than masking it — a classic pairing.
friendly: That crisp acidity just lifts the {dish} right up, it's a classic match for a reason.
luxury: The wine's acidity is a natural foil for seafood — it lifts the dish instead of sitting on top of it.

entries.principle: lightness matches lightness: keeps a delicate/light dish from feeling weighed down
entries.rotation: deterministic-hash (single-variant clause set, no rotation needed)

professional: A lighter white keeps the plate feeling fresh rather than weighed down.
friendly: Keeps things light, the wine won't bulldoze the {dish} at all.
luxury: A lighter-bodied white lets the more delicate notes in the {dish} come through.

entries.principle: carbonation cuts richness and adds a celebratory lift

professional: The bubbles cut through the richness and keep every bite feeling fresh.
friendly: Bubbles always cut through a plate like this, it keeps things feeling fresh — and it's got a nice celebratory lift too.
luxury: The bead in the wine cuts cleanly through the dish and lifts the whole course.

entries.principle: mid-weight balance: enough body for the dish, stays light enough not to weigh the table down
entries.rotation: deterministic-hash (single-variant clause set, no rotation needed)

professional: It has enough body for the dish but stays light enough not to weigh the table down.
friendly: It's got just enough weight for the {dish} without feeling heavy.
luxury: There's enough structure here for the dish, without ever feeling heavy-handed.

entries.principle: chicken is forgiving; keeping the drink light keeps the whole plate balanced and lets delicate cooking show
entries.fidelity_note: Cross-cutting rule: matches ANY light-bodied drink OR any white wine, not wine exclusively. Placed here because white wine is the clearest wine-domain instance of this rule.

professional: Chicken is forgiving, but a lighter pour keeps the whole plate feeling balanced.
friendly: Chicken goes with almost anything, but keeping it light like this keeps the whole plate balanced.
luxury: A lighter pour lets the more delicate cooking on the chicken still come through.
